newsitem.title: USA: Calif. localities to join BankAmerica bond suits.
newsitem.headline: Calif. localities to join BankAmerica bond suits.

text.p: At least 15 local governments in California plan to join lawsuits filed against BankAmerica Corp for allegedly mismanaging municipal bond funds, a lead attorney in the case said on Thursday.

The lawsuits, which were filed in San Francisco Superior Court, allege that BankAmerica unit Bank of America overcharged issuers, failed to return unclaimed funds from bond trust accounts, and improperly invested funds from some of the accounts.

A Bank of America spokesperson was not immediately available to comment. Bank of America maintains that the investments it made were appropriate, and that it has fully returned unclaimed funds from the bond accounts.
The 15 local governments will be joining lawsuits filed in May by San Francisco and the state of California against the bank, San Francisco Deputy City Attorney Matt Davis said.

They include the California counties of Santa Cruz, Alameda and Nevada, as well as the cities of Belmont, Burbank, Ventura, Folsom, Santa Rosa, Richmond, Foster City and San Bernardino, Davis told Reuters.
Burbank's redevelopment agency, San Diego's water district, San Bernardino's redevelopment agency and San Bernardino's water department will also join the case.
Davis said the 15 complaints would be filed in Superior Court in the coming days. Other local governments may also take part, he said.

Last week, the counties of Riverside, Marin, Contra Costa, Santa Clara, Sonoma, Solano and Tulare filed complaints, along with the city of Industry, the Industry Urban-Development Agency and the East Stockton Municipal Water District, according to court documents.
The lawsuits were based on a so-called "whistleblower" complaint filed under seal in April 1995 by Patrick Stull, a former vice president for corporate trust at Bank of America.
